headline: Regional Permits and Seasonal Access for the Southern Highlands
reservation: Reservations for developed campgrounds in the Ocoee or Tellico districts must be made through official federal booking platforms, with windows often opening six months in advance. While general forest entry is free, certain high-impact recreation areas require a daily pass or fee. Always check the USDA Forest Service website for current road closures and permit requirements for specific river activities.

days.title: Rivers and Vistas of the South

stops.name: Bald River Falls
stops.detail: View this landmark waterfall from the bridge, checking official road status for construction detours beforehand.

stops.name: Cherohala Skyway Overlooks
stops.detail: Stop at designated high-elevation pullouts for views of the Unaka Mountains along this scenic ridge drive.

days.driving: Allow 3 hours for the Skyway loop; mountain grades can be steep.
days.note: Fog can significantly reduce visibility at high elevations; check weather forecasts.

days.title: Paddling and Peaks

stops.name: Parksville Lake
stops.detail: Use the Chilhowee Recreation Area for lake access, swimming, or a shoreline picnic.

stops.name: Benton Falls
stops.detail: Hike the manageable trail from the Chilhowee plateau to reach this tiered waterfall.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour between lake access and trailhead parking.
days.note: Ensure you use designated parking; US 64 shoulders are narrow and high-traffic.

days.title: Whitewater and History

stops.name: Ocoee Whitewater Center
stops.detail: Explore the legacy of the Olympic course and walk the riverside trails; check for water release schedules.

stops.name: Old Copper Hill Museum
stops.detail: Visit the gateway area to understand the region's industrial mining history and landscape recovery.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local transfers between Ocoee sites.
days.note: River swimming is not permitted in the whitewater sections; use designated lake areas.

intel.title: Ocoee Corridor Constraints
intel.text: Parking at popular waterfall trailheads and the Whitewater Center fills rapidly on summer weekends. Use only designated lots to avoid citations and traffic hazards along the river highway.

intel.title: Highland Dead Zones
intel.text: Cellular coverage drops significantly on the Cherohala Skyway and deep within the Tellico River corridor. Carry physical maps and notify contacts of your route before entering the forest.

intel.title: Gateway Fill-ups
intel.text: Fuel is unavailable on the 40-mile stretch of the Cherohala Skyway. Refill in Tellico Plains or Robbinsville before starting the mountain ascent.

intel.title: Dam Release Schedules
intel.text: Flow levels on the Ocoee River are controlled by dam releases for power and recreation. Check the official Tennessee Valley Authority or outfitter calendars for specific whitewater dates.

intel.title: Road Closures
intel.text: High-elevation roads and campgrounds may close seasonally due to ice or storm damage. Consult the Forest Service alerts page for the Southern District before your departure.

plan.arrival: Arrive at TRI or TYS, secure a rental, and obtain supplies in Elizabethton or Tellico Plains depending on your chosen district.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are fine for main scenic byways, but gravel forest roads may require AWD; check rental terms for unpaved roads.
plan.goldenHour: The Cherohala Skyway overlooks offer spectacular sunset views, though mountain weather can obscure the horizon unexpectedly.
